title: Hardware accelerated UI rendering broken (Sony Vaio VPCCA2S0E gen6 gt2)
body: Following a recent Nightly update, the whole Firefox UI renders unreadably as soon as I start it (screenshot attached); turning hardware acceleration off renders fine (reference screenshot attached). Reproduces with a fresh profile (mozregression-gui). So far I've only tried 32-bit Firefox. Hardware is a Sony Vaio VPCCA2S0E with Intel gen6 gt2 (SandyBridge HD3000) graphics. I already bisected: first broken build is 1c58e874, and the change that caused it looks like bug 1823578 (D173095). I also poked gfx.webrender prefs one at a time: gfx.webrender.use-optimized-shaders=false fixes it, gfx.webrender.software=true fixes it, nine other webrender prefs have no effect. Troubleshooting report (fresh profile, JSON) attached.

symptoms_visible: The entire Firefox UI renders unreadably as soon as Firefox starts with hardware acceleration enabled; disabling hardware acceleration renders correctly.
Reproduces on a fresh profile with no add-ons (via mozregression-gui); only 32-bit Firefox tried so far.
N0.label: N0 expert report with self-bisection

symptoms_visible: After updating to the Nightly containing the clip-mask revert, more of the UI works (notably many buttons), but backgrounds and text-on-background compositing are still the wrong colour; text can be invisible (same colour as background).
Disabling optimized shaders still fixes rendering on this build.
N1_x.label: N1_x partial-fix aftermath

symptoms_visible: The provided try builds (32-bit and 64-bit) that revert more of the shader change still show the broken background rendering (verified in a blank test profile, build 20230507194423).
N2_x.label: N2_x revert-more measurement outcome

symptoms_visible: Broken background rendering persists in default configuration; workarounds (optimized shaders off, or software WebRender) both render correctly.
N3.label: N3 device-scoped decision ready

symptoms_visible: UI renders correctly on the updated Nightly with default settings; about:support shows WEBRENDER_OPTIMIZED_SHADERS blocklisted due to known issues: bug 1829487.
N_terminal.label: terminal resolved

solution.intent: Update to the latest Nightly containing the clip-mask rendering revert (bug 1830691), expected to temporarily resolve the corruption.
solution.concrete_example: This should be temporarily resolved when bug 1830691 lands — please confirm on the most recent Nightly with config settings reverted to their previous values.

edges.comment: Real thread c19-c25: the revert improved parts of the UI but backgrounds/text compositing stayed broken; case answer key marks this as a known non-resolving fix attempt with a symptom-evolving aftermath. The Nightly update changes the user's system (S1 -> S1b). The bisected first-broken build 1c58e874 being the RELANDED shader change is engineer-side reading (c13-c14).

question_patterns: Here is a try build that reverts more of the base shader change — could you run it and check whether backgrounds render correctly?
Please test the linked target.zip (32-bit or 64-bit) in a blank profile and report the result.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Both zip files (32-bit and 64-bit) still show the problem. I made a blank profile for testing; both report version 20230507194423.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The revert build renders everything correctly on both architectures.

edges.comment: Real thread c26-c30: a handler-provided diagnostic try build the user runs purely to see what it shows — a measurement, reclassified from a blind solution edge per the measurement-class rule. The falsified fix attempt of this case remains e1.

question_patterns: Is the 2016-era graphics driver on your machine the most recent available for that GPU?
Can you check whether Intel still publishes driver updates for this gen6 chip?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Pretty sure this is the latest: the processor is 2nd-generation Intel Core and end-of-life. Intel's site lists 9.17.10.4229 (2015) as the latest; I run 9.17.10.4459, likely a manufacturer variant.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Intel actually shipped a 2023 driver update for this GPU with shader compiler fixes; the machine is several versions behind.
The laptop's battery is also failing and it runs on mains power only.

question_patterns: How does browser performance feel on your machine with gfx.webrender.software enabled?
Could you compare default hardware rendering, optimized-shaders-off, and software WebRender on a graphics benchmark?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Ran MotionMark 1.2 on latest Nightly: overall 135.67 ±8.59% on default h/w, 140.15 ±7.74% with optimized shaders off, 99.84 ±8.25% on software WebRender; the pre-regression build scores 133.46, Chrome 137.85, Edge 150.29 (first distorted run discarded). The difference between full hardware acceleration and skipping shader optimisation is within the run-to-run variation.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Software WebRender scores indistinguishably from hardware rendering on this machine across the whole benchmark.

edges.comment: Real thread c31-c39: device-scoping questions that justify a blocklist scoped to optimized shaders (keep hardware WebRender) instead of forcing SWGL fallback for the whole device class. The benchmark numbers and the within-variation conclusion are the reporter's own (c39).

solution.intent: Block the shader-optimization feature on Windows + SandyBridge via the gfx blocklist (keeping hardware WebRender enabled), verify on a provided test build, then update to the Nightly carrying the blocklist entry.
solution.concrete_example: Land 'Block shader optimization feature on Windows + SandyBridge'; reporter verifies the follow-up try build renders correctly, then confirms on the next Nightly where about:support shows WEBRENDER_OPTIMIZED_SHADERS blocklisted (bug 1829487).

edges.comment: Resolution per c33-c44: device-scoped blocklist chosen over full hw-wr block; interim fix landed, long-term shader-optimizer fix tracked separately.

solution.inference_hint: Proposing the device-scoped blocklist directly from the filing-time evidence (self-bisection: optimized-shaders-off fixes it; EOL SandyBridge hardware) is a shortcut; displayed reasoning must cover why the scope is the shader-optimizer path on this device class, acknowledging the driver/perf evidence it skips.

edges.comment: Hand-authored canonical exit from N0: the real thread's first move was the falsified clip-mask suggestion, but the case answer (blocklist optimized shaders on SandyBridge) is proposable at filing time as a displayed-inference shortcut. Cross-state (S1 vs S1b) so the expander cannot plant this copy itself.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the root cause class: the optimized-shader path from the relanded shader change miscompiles on the end-of-life Intel SandyBridge (gen6 gt2 / HD3000) driver via ANGLE->D3D11; this is device/driver-specific, not a general WebRender failure.

The final fix must be scoped to the affected device class (blocklist optimized shaders on SandyBridge) rather than disabling hardware acceleration or WebRender globally, using the performance-comparison evidence to justify the scope.

Must build on the reporter's self-collected evidence (pref bisection, regression window) and must not re-propose the already-falsified move (the clip-mask-revert update); the broader-revert try build was a diagnostic measurement whose negative result must be respected.
Must have the reporter verify on a test build or updated Nightly (blocklist entry visible in about:support) before treating the issue as resolved.

persona_hint.experience_level: Expert power user: ran mozregression and a one-at-a-time pref bisection before filing; comfortable with try builds, blank test profiles and benchmarks; runs 32-bit Firefox on end-of-life hardware.
persona_hint.communication_style: Precise and proactive; states exactly what was tested and on which build IDs; volunteers structured evidence; notes own timezone constraints for testing turnaround.
